Quick summary of options (Private / VPC):
- Data residency: customer-controlled AWS region; live data and primary backups remain in-region by default.
- Retention: platform default retention is configurable per-customer. Common starting points: 0 days (no storage beyond request), 90 days, or custom SLR.
- Deletion: support for immediate in-region purge via API + secure scrub of caches; backup destruction is handled on a schedule (see Neha).
- Redaction/tokenization: we offer ingestion-time PII redaction (configurable rules) and a tokenization workflow for PHI-sensitive fields.

Hi all — quick technical breakdown and what we typically produce for HIPAA customers. Mark, I kept it concise below; happy to expand on any point on a call.

1) Region & replication
- For Private (VPC) deployments, we bind primary storage to the AWS region the customer specifies.
- We do not replicate customer snapshots to other regions unless a cross-region DR option is explicitly requested and contractually authorized.

2) Encryption & key control
- All data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. For Private customers we offer BYOK via KMS/HSM where keys live in the customer's AWS account (recommended for PHI).
- Transit encryption is TLS 1.2+; internal inter-service comms use mTLS.

3) Retention semantics
- Platform has three retention surfaces: live request store, KV/inference cache, and backups/snapshots.
- Live store retention is configurable per workspace. Default templates are: immediate (0 days), 30, 90, 365. We can enforce a maximum retention policy per contract.
- Cache entries (KV) are normally purged within 24–72 hours unless pinned by a long-running session; we provide an API to force eviction.

4) Deletion & proof
- Deletion flow: (a) mark and purge live records via the purge API (audit log entry), (b) invalidate and overwrite KV cache entries, (c) schedule snapshot lifecycle deletion — snapshots are marked for deletion immediately and then destroyed per cloud provider lifecycle (typically within 24–72 hours for object lifecycle + eventual background shredding), (d) logs containing PII/PHI are subject to our platform logging retention policy but can be redacted or excluded upon contract.
- Proof-of-deletion: we provide a signed attest with timestamps for live-store purge and cache eviction. For backups we provide lifecycle logs showing object deletion events and manifest checksums. For higher-assurance needs we can coordinate HSM key rotation + crypto-erase of backups when keys are customer-controlled.

5) Redaction & tokenization options
- Ingestion-time redaction: configurable regex / entity rules that remove or mask fields before persistent storage.
- Tokenization: we support a token vault mode where tokens replace PHI and original values are stored in a customer-controlled secret store or external token service.
- Post-hoc redaction: we can run a one-off redaction job against existing data, but it requires an ingestion snapshot and has an operational window (we'll provide OTP/manifest for verification).

6) Backups / DR behavior
- Backups live in the same AWS region by default. Cross-region replication is opt-in and requires explicit contract language.
- Backup retention schedules are configurable; default retention for snapshots is 30–90 days depending on chosen plan.

7) Evidence & artifacts we can provide
- HIPAA security statement PDF (attached)
- Retention matrix (attached)
- Signed deletion attestations and S3 object delete logs on request
- SOC2 report (redacted) and penetration test summaries available under NDA

Operational notes / recommended configuration for PHI pilot:
- Recommend Private deployment with BYOK (customer KMS) + ingestion-time tokenization on PHI fields.
- Set live retention to 90 days, enable immediate KV eviction on session end, and request monthly snapshot purge (or 'on-demand' if required).
- Add contract clause for backup crypto-erase by rotating customer keys if you require absolute inability to recover.
